_COMMENTS: ================ EXPLANATIONS BELOW (not read as settings, just notes for you) ================
_comment_paths: pose_task_path / hand_task_path / onnx_model_path / label_map_path -- only change if you move/rename model files. Relative to main.py's folder.
_comment_fixed_len: fixed_len -- frames per prediction window. Must match model training. Do NOT change unless you retrain.
_comment_confidence_threshold: confidence_threshold -- min model confidence (0-1) to consider a prediction. Higher = fewer false detections but may miss real signs. Lower = catches more but noisier.
_comment_speech_mode: speech_mode -- controls what gets spoken. 'words_and_sentences' = speak every sign AND full sentences on match. 'sentence_only' = silent on single signs, only speak on a full template match. 'words_only' = speak every sign, never match sentences.
_comment_tts_rate: tts_rate -- text-to-speech speaking speed (approx words per minute). Higher = faster/rushed, lower = slower/clearer.
_comment_camera_index: camera_index -- which camera device to open. 0 = default/first camera. If wrong camera opens, try 1, 2, etc.
_comment_stability_frames: stability_frames -- consecutive same-prediction frames needed to confirm a sign. Higher = fewer false positives but slower reaction (sign must be held longer). Lower = faster reaction but more misfires.
_comment_same_sign_cooldown_frames: same_sign_cooldown_frames -- frames to ignore repeats of the SAME sign after it's confirmed, so one held sign isn't re-confirmed repeatedly. Higher = safer against duplicates but may miss genuine fast repeats. Lower = catches repeats faster but risks double-firing on a held sign.
_comment_word_buffer_size: word_buffer_size -- how many recent confirmed signs are kept for sentence matching. Should be >= your longest template in sentence_templates.py.
_comment_word_buffer_timeout_seconds: word_buffer_timeout_seconds -- if no new sign is confirmed within this many seconds, the word buffer auto-clears. Prevents a stale half-finished word (e.g. you signed 'look' but never followed up) from sitting around and accidentally completing a sentence much later. Lower = clears faster/stricter, higher = more forgiving of pauses between signs.
_comment_confusable_pairs: confusable_pairs -- pairs of signs that look visually similar to the model and can get mixed up (e.g. thankyou vs talk both start near the mouth/chin). For any pair listed here, the top prediction must beat the runner-up by confusable_margin or the frame is ignored as 'unclear' instead of wrongly confirmed. Add more pairs as needed: [['signA','signB'], ['signC','signD']].
_comment_confusable_margin: confusable_margin -- minimum probability gap (0-1) required between top and second prediction for a confusable pair to be accepted. Higher = stricter, fewer mix-ups but more 'unclear, try again' moments. Lower = more lenient, may let mix-ups back in.
_comment_label_overrides: label_overrides -- relabel a predicted sign to a different output word everywhere (on-screen text, voice, sentence buffer). Format is a list, one override per line: "predicted_word": "output_word". Example with several: {"talk": "thankyou", "wake": "awake", "who": "hello"} means talk shows as thankyou, wake shows as awake, who shows as hello. All OTHER signs not listed are unaffected and output normally as trained. A direct 'thankyou' prediction still outputs 'thankyou' as usual -- overrides don't chain. Set to {} to disable and use raw model output for every sign.
_comment_process_interval_ms: NEW: How often (in milliseconds) the prediction loop runs. Lower = faster response but more CPU usage. Default 40 (25 FPS).
_comment_prefer_webgpu_onnx: prefer_webgpu_onnx -- if true, ONNX inference tries WebGPU first and automatically falls back to WASM if it's unavailable or fails (this fallback is solid, both at startup and if it starts erroring mid-session). Default true.
_comment_prefer_gpu_mediapipe: prefer_gpu_mediapipe -- if true, the hand/pose detectors try the GPU delegate first before falling back to CPU. Default FALSE on purpose: unlike the ONNX path, a broken GPU delegate can initialize successfully but then silently produce weak/empty landmarks on some hardware without ever throwing an error, so there's no reliable signal to auto-fall-back on. CPU delegate is slower but has proven reliable. Only flip this to true if you've verified GPU detection actually works well on your target hardware.
